system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your gap_45 and gap_56
codes specifically. Cite ONLY closing-structure evidence; do NOT reason about later
outcomes.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: inability to determine a
structural field is "uncertain"; a gap you cannot document at closing is 0.

# Structural sub-dossier — Apollo Group / The Carlyle Group formation of Apollo Global, Inc. (closing structure)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY how the
> transaction was structured at formation — what crossed the ownership boundary and what
> did not. It contains no post-transaction outcome information.

## The drawn filing (described truthfully)
- The drawn filing is Apollo Group, Inc.'s Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year
  ended August 31, 2009; it is a periodic annual report, not the instrument that formed
  or set the terms of the entity described below, but it narrates that entity's structure
  as of fiscal 2009. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- The formation-era structure is additionally sourced from the registrant's contemporaneous
  Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2008, the first annual report covering the
  period in which the entity was formed. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]

## Parties and vehicle at formation
- In October 2007 Apollo Group, Inc. and The Carlyle Group established Apollo Global, Inc.
  as a jointly owned entity ("a joint venture with The Carlyle Group") to pursue investments
  primarily in the international education-services industry. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]
- The vehicle is a distinct corporate entity, Apollo Global, Inc.; Carlyle is described as
  one of the world's largest private-equity firms, contributing as a minority financial
  partner. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]

## Ownership, governance and capital as structured
- At formation the parties agreed to commit up to $801 million (Apollo Group, for 80.1%
  ownership) and up to $199 million (Carlyle, for the remaining 19.9%), in cash or
  contributed assets. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]
- As of August 31, 2008, total cash contributions to Apollo Global were $61.0 million, of
  which $48.9 million was funded by Apollo Group; the entity was consolidated in Apollo
  Group's financial statements. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]
- As of August 31, 2009, Apollo Group owned 86.1% and Carlyle owned 13.9%; total cash
  contributions were approximately $511.8 million, of which $440.5 million was funded by
  Apollo Group; the entity remained consolidated (controlled) in Apollo Group's financial
  statements. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]

## What crossed the boundary — customer-facing product, processes, people
- The entity acquired operating, accredited institutions as going concerns, each retaining
  its accreditations, trademarks, campuses and local operations: UNIACC (Chile, purchased
  March 2008), Universidad Latinoamericana / ULA (Mexico, 65% August 2008, remaining
  interest July 2009), and BPP Holdings plc (United Kingdom, acquired July 30, 2009). [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- BPP is described as a provider of professional education and training organized into three
  operating divisions (Professional Education; College of Professional Studies operating four
  law schools, a business school and HR training; and Mander Portman Woodward), delivering
  through UK schools and a European office network — i.e. the customer-facing product, its
  delivering operations and its organization transferred together as an intact institution. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- The acquired institutions were run as their own reportable segments (Apollo Global — BPP;
  Apollo Global — Other, which includes UNIACC, ULA and Apollo Global corporate operations),
  and BPP's operating results were consolidated from its acquisition date. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- For BPP, the purchase consideration comprised $506.459 million cash paid, $84.306 million
  debt assumed and $10.821 million transaction-related costs; the acquisition recorded
  $425.6 million of goodwill and $191.294 million of acquired intangibles (including
  $134.068 million trademarks and $5.922 million accreditations and designations, both
  assigned indefinite lives). [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]

## Bridging / shared-substrate arrangements at formation
- No transitional-services, shared-services or supply agreement bridging a shared operating
  substrate between Apollo Group and the acquired institutions is described in the drawn or
  contemporaneous filings reviewed; the acquired institutions are presented as self-standing
  operating segments rather than businesses dependent on a retained parent substrate. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]

## Structural summary (formation only)
- Two parties formed a jointly owned corporate vehicle (Apollo Group majority/controlling,
  Carlyle minority financial partner) capitalized by staged cash/asset commitments, through
  which they acquired operating accredited institutions as going concerns — each carrying its
  customer-facing programs together with its delivering operations, trademarks, accreditations
  and organization — run as distinct consolidated reportable segments. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009] [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]

[SLICE END]

# Structural sub-dossier — Apollo Group / The Carlyle Group formation of Apollo Global, Inc. (closing structure)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`

## The drawn filing (described truthfully)
- The drawn filing is Apollo Group, Inc.'s Form 10-K annual report for the fiscal year
  ended August 31, 2009; it is a periodic annual report, not the instrument that formed
  or set the terms of the entity described below, but it narrates that entity's structure
  as of fiscal 2009. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- The formation-era structure is additionally sourced from the registrant's contemporaneous
  Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2008, the first annual report covering the
  period in which the entity was formed. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]

## Parties and vehicle at formation
- In October 2007 Apollo Group, Inc. and The Carlyle Group established Apollo Global, Inc.
  as a jointly owned entity ("a joint venture with The Carlyle Group") to pursue investments
  primarily in the international education-services industry. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]
- The vehicle is a distinct corporate entity, Apollo Global, Inc.; Carlyle is described as
  one of the world's largest private-equity firms, contributing as a minority financial
  partner. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]

## Ownership, governance and capital as structured
- At formation the parties agreed to commit up to $801 million (Apollo Group, for 80.1%
  ownership) and up to $199 million (Carlyle, for the remaining 19.9%), in cash or
  contributed assets. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]
- As of August 31, 2008, total cash contributions to Apollo Global were $61.0 million, of
  which $48.9 million was funded by Apollo Group; the entity was consolidated in Apollo
  Group's financial statements. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]
- As of August 31, 2009, Apollo Group owned 86.1% and Carlyle owned 13.9%; total cash
  contributions were approximately $511.8 million, of which $440.5 million was funded by
  Apollo Group; the entity remained consolidated (controlled) in Apollo Group's financial
  statements. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]

## What crossed the boundary — customer-facing product, processes, people
- The entity acquired operating, accredited institutions as going concerns, each retaining
  its accreditations, trademarks, campuses and local operations: UNIACC (Chile, purchased
  March 2008), Universidad Latinoamericana / ULA (Mexico, 65% August 2008, remaining
  interest July 2009), and BPP Holdings plc (United Kingdom, acquired July 30, 2009). [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- BPP is described as a provider of professional education and training organized into three
  operating divisions (Professional Education; College of Professional Studies operating four
  law schools, a business school and HR training; and Mander Portman Woodward), delivering
  through UK schools and a European office network — i.e. the customer-facing product, its
  delivering operations and its organization transferred together as an intact institution. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- The acquired institutions were run as their own reportable segments (Apollo Global — BPP;
  Apollo Global — Other, which includes UNIACC, ULA and Apollo Global corporate operations),
  and BPP's operating results were consolidated from its acquisition date. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]
- For BPP, the purchase consideration comprised $506.459 million cash paid, $84.306 million
  debt assumed and $10.821 million transaction-related costs; the acquisition recorded
  $425.6 million of goodwill and $191.294 million of acquired intangibles (including
  $134.068 million trademarks and $5.922 million accreditations and designations, both
  assigned indefinite lives). [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]

## Bridging / shared-substrate arrangements at formation
- No transitional-services, shared-services or supply agreement bridging a shared operating
  substrate between Apollo Group and the acquired institutions is described in the drawn or
  contemporaneous filings reviewed; the acquired institutions are presented as self-standing
  operating segments rather than businesses dependent on a retained parent substrate. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009]

## Structural summary (formation only)
- Two parties formed a jointly owned corporate vehicle (Apollo Group majority/controlling,
  Carlyle minority financial partner) capitalized by staged cash/asset commitments, through
  which they acquired operating accredited institutions as going concerns — each carrying its
  customer-facing programs together with its delivering operations, trademarks, accreditations
  and organization — run as distinct consolidated reportable segments. [SRC: SEC accession 0000950123-09-053647, Form 10-K FY2009] [SRC: SEC accession 0000950153-08-001796, Form 10-K FY2008]

[SLICE END]
